parts.title: My grandmother's cafe
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
My grandmother opened her cafe forty years ago, on a corner near the market. At first, it had only four tables, and she made everything herself: the soup, the sandwiches and the apple cake that people still talk about.

When I was a child, I spent every summer there. I washed cups, carried plates and listened to the customers. There was an old man who came every morning at eight and ordered a black coffee, and a group of students who argued about films for hours. My grandmother knew every name, and she remembered how everybody liked their drinks.

Last year, she became ill and thought about selling the cafe. I did not want that to happen, so I took a break from university to help. It was harder than I had expected. I got up at five to bake, and my feet hurt by the afternoon.

Now business is better than ever. We have added a small shelf of second-hand books, and customers can borrow one while they drink their coffee. My grandmother visits every day, sits at her favourite table and tells me that the cake is not as good as hers. She is probably right.

questions.explanation: People still talk about her apple cake.

questions.explanation: She washed cups, carried plates and listened to customers.

parts.title: A short history of coffee
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Coffee has a long and interesting history. [1] According to an old story, a farmer in Ethiopia noticed that his goats became very lively after eating the red berries of a certain bush.

At first, people ate the berries or chewed the leaves. [2] Slowly, the habit of drinking coffee spread across the Arab world, where the first coffee houses opened.

In the seventeenth century, traders brought coffee to Europe. [3] Many people thought it was a dangerous drink, but soon cafes appeared in every big city.

These cafes became meeting places. [4] Writers, artists and business people spent hours there, talking and reading the news.

Today, coffee is one of the most traded goods in the world. [5] For many people, a day cannot begin without a cup.
sentences: It was a completely new taste for most of them.
Over two billion cups are drunk every day.
Later, someone had the idea of making a hot drink from the beans.
Tea is much more popular in some countries.
Nobody knows exactly who first discovered it.
People could hear new ideas and share them for the price of a cup.

gaps.explanation: Nobody knows who discovered it; the next sentence gives an old story.
People first ate berries; later they made a hot drink from the beans.
It was a new taste; the next sentence says many people thought it was dangerous.
Cafes were meeting places where people shared ideas; the next sentence lists writers and artists.
Billions of cups are drunk every day; the next sentence says people cannot start the day without one.

parts.title: A talk by a cafe owner
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: owner
turns.text: Welcome to my cafe, everybody. I am Aldis, and I started this business five years ago. I want to tell you a little about how we work. We open at half past seven, and the first customers are usually people on their way to work. By ten o'clock, we have sold about a hundred coffees. Our most popular cake is the lemon cake, which we make every morning. We buy our milk from a farm that is only ten kilometres away. On Wednesdays, we run a book club in the back room, and about twelve people come. If you would like to work here, we need someone at weekends. The pay is eight pounds an hour, and you get a free lunch. Please leave your name at the counter.

gaps.explanation: He says he started the business five years ago.

gaps.explanation: He says they open at half past seven.

gaps.prompt: The most popular cake is the ___ cake
gaps.explanation: He says the lemon cake is the most popular.

gaps.prompt: The milk comes from a farm ___ kilometres away
gaps.explanation: He says the farm is ten kilometres away.
He says they run a book club on Wednesdays.
He says you get a free lunch.

parts.title: An interview with a tea taster
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Dante, you taste tea for a living. How did you start?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: My grandmother had a tea shop. As a boy, I loved the smell of the leaves, and she let me help to mix them.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What does a tea taster actually do?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I taste about two hundred cups a day. I make a note of the colour, the smell and the flavour, and then I decide which teas to buy.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you swallow all that tea?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: No, I spit it out, like a wine taster. Otherwise, I would not sleep for a week!

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the secret of a good cup?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Fresh water and the right time. Most people leave the bag in for too long, and the tea becomes bitter. Three minutes is enough for black tea.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you drink tea at home?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Of course, but I like it simple, with a little milk. I save the special teas for my friends.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice would you give to someone starting out?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Be patient. It takes years to train your nose and your tongue.
